pr_title: fix(core): only try to retrieve transferred state on the browser
pr_body:
Prior to this commit we tried to retrieve transferred state on both browser and server. Doing this on the server was redundant and could causes issues as `document` might be undefined.

Closes #50138

issue_context.title: Angular 16 migration: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getElementById')
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

Don't known / other

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

Migrating from angular 15.2.9 to 16.0.0 we encounter the stack trace below when running the universal server (dev & prod build).
spa dev mode works as expected without any noticeable issues. 
Following the stack trace it's this piece of code that is encountering an issue:
```js
function retrieveTransferredState(doc,appId){const script=doc.getElementById(appId+"-state");
```
The error occurs whether we provide client hydration or not. 
We use TransferState throughout the application to send data from ssr to the client. 

EnvironmentService, that seems to be the root of this error, injects TransferState in the constructor.

I don't quite know how to drill down on this issue, since this seems to be happening very early in app lifecycle. Any Idea on how to create a reproduction would be highly appreciated.

comments:
The line mentioned is failing https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/2419c486ad8a3129d27ade6852e33d1435512da1/packages/core/src/transfer_state.ts#LL75C50-L75C61, this is because `getDocument` can return `undefined` (might make sense to change this to a throw.)

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/2419c486ad8a3129d27ade6852e33d1435512da1/packages/core/src/render3/interfaces/document.ts#L44-L56

The question however is why in your case the `document` is not being set on the server, which happens when using the `ServerModule`. https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/2419c486ad8a3129d27ade6852e33d1435512da1/packages/platform-server/src/server.ts#L68-L80

I would start by looking at how the application is bootstrapped on the server and verify that `ServerModule` is being imported.

Thank you for the hints! I managed to triage the error.
The root cause is our Custom ErrorHandler that injects the EnvironmentService. We pass version + environment information through TransferState to the ErrorHandler to be able to annotate our error reports client side.

I've created a minimal reproduction here:
https://github.com/MarcoGlauser/16-migration-repro
Specifically this commit to see where the issue happens:
https://github.com/MarcoGlauser/16-migration-repro/commit/4225768a2552fd9be347bb5f90694383b479ff28

I managed to fix the issue for us by marking DOCUMENT as dependency to the provider in question:
```
deps: [DOCUMENT]
```
However, this was not required with previous versions of Angular.

Digging some more, the problem here is that `TransferState` has an implicate dependency on `DOCUMENT`. Which is not defined in https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/2419c486ad8a3129d27ade6852e33d1435512da1/packages/core/src/transfer_state.ts#LL75C50-L75C61. The main reason for this is that the `DOCUMENT` token is defined in `@angular/common`, and hence why `getDocument` is being used here. 

Let me have a chat with @AndrewKushnir  later today about this.
